items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Later I got to know the other musicians who were Edgar Sampson, alto sax, Happy Cauldwell, a little fellow with a big voice and big tone on tenor sax; George Washington, trombone, Paul Barnet, banjo, and Billy Taylor, the tuba man

ctx.x: I was standing by a railing just in front of the two band stands where I could see and hear everything that happened and when Fess had finished his set, the other orchestra came on. Both orchestras had their names above their stands and this orchestra was under the leadership of Arthur Gibbs. I had never seen or heard about these musicians but when they started their first number, I knew that it was an orchestra that had something to say, and during their set they said plenty. There was one trumpet player who…

When Arthur finished his set, they came off and I left my place to go and find the trumpet player. I told him my name, and that I was a trumpet player and it was my first night to New York. Also, that I liked his playing very much. He told me that his name was Leonard Davis. Later I got to know the other musicians who were Edgar Sampson, alto sax, Happy Cauldwell, a little fellow with a big voice and big tone on tenor sax; George Washington, trombone, Paul Barnet, banjo, and Billy Taylor, the tuba man
The drummer was Ralph..... I don't remember his last name, nor the name of the other alto.
